description.purpose: The one cell in the tree with an edge onto the mutation door, and a store beside it that is its whole memory. It takes a manifest that somebody drafted, checks that its bytes are the ones the digest was drawn over, takes the requester's identity off the ENVELOPE rather than out of the body -- and then ASKS. Who may submit is a question for the capability broker, put once per submission over the manifest's scope root and in the check-only form, while the manifest itself waits parked in the store under its own digest. Since 2.1.0 there is a SECOND question when the diff asks for one: a manifest carrying a script override or an `add_templates` is asking to author executable behaviour, and `code.author` is asked over the same root before anything is un-parked. Since 2.2.0 there is a THIRD, and it is the reason for the second digit: an `add_edges` entry whose modifier re-stamps an arriving message onto the `in_pack` lane is a brain subscribing to its own identity, so the gate checks the FORM of that edge itself -- it must start at an affinity hive and end at the requester's own hive or at a node the same declaration creates, both read RESOLVED against that declaration's scope -- and asks the broker `affinity.subscribe` for the permission. Three questions, one parked row, one digest, asked in sequence. A permitted manifest is un-parked, stamped with its attribution and emitted ONCE on `mutate`. The colony's answer comes back directly, in a fresh trace that carries no correlation at all -- so a second row is what tells it whose round this was, and the receipt goes out stamped with that call's id. Since 2.2.1 the receipt carries the door's own `details` behind the position and the class: the colony computes a reason for every refusal, and a requester -- or a composer's repair round -- told only the class repairs blind. Since 2.3.0 the receipt also says what the DIFF asked for and not only what the door did: `hop.registers_class` is `true` on every receipt whose manifest carried an `add_templates`, `false` on every other one, and it is REMEMBERED on the flight row rather than read off the answer -- the colony replies on a fresh trace that carries no diff at all. One boolean, so an edge can test for "this submission registered a class" without opening a body; the caller it exists for is the shell that nudges the baumeister's corpus when one does (#504). Since 2.3.1 the created-node branch verifies its own anchor before it trusts it: a name in `add_nodes` counts as an addressee this declaration brings into the world only when the entry INSTANTIATES -- a `template` or an `adopt` block, the door's two mutually exclusive shapes -- and only when the name lies under the declaration's own scope, segment-wise. An entry that carries neither brings no addressee into the world, and a name outside the scope addresses somebody else's tree; either way it anchors nothing, so the edge is refused by form with `subscribe_target_not_self` instead of falling through to the permissive read. A security default does not lean on a later stage for the shape of its own anchor (#566).
description.use_when: Once per colony, at the OS level, beside the builder that drafts -- and NOT inside it. The guardrail of R6 is a missing edge, and a missing edge can only be missing between two nodes.
description.not_in_scope: No drafting, no composing, no model, no disk, no network -- and no policy of its own. It does not decide WHO may submit, it does not decide whether this manifest may AUTHOR CODE, it does not decide whether an identity may SUBSCRIBE, and it does not decide WHAT is applied. It DERIVES the second and third questions from the diff and asks them -- and it decides exactly one thing on its own, the FORM of a subscribe edge, because that is the one half no policy row can state: everything it emits was handed to it, byte for byte, by somebody whose identity the substrate stamped, and permitted by somebody else.
examples: a manifest whose bytes changed on the way through a chat -> `manifest_digest_mismatch`, and nothing is parked and nothing is asked

two declarations under `/os/orgs/acme` and `/os/orgs/acme/members` -> ONE question, about `/os/orgs/acme`; two under `/os/orgs/acme` and `/os/orgs/beta` ask about `/os/orgs`, which is stricter and never more permissive
the broker says no -> `requester_not_permitted`, the same string this template has always used, and the parked row goes with the refusal
the broker does not answer a readable verdict -> `submission_check_failed`, and nothing reaches the door: the one cell with that edge does not guess
the colony answers `{"outcome": "rejected", "applied": 2, "failed_at": 3}` -> a receipt that says WHERE it stopped and how much is live now, because a manifest has no rollback
a tool call `c2` asks for the apply -> the receipt comes back as a `tool_result` whose id IS `c2`, taken off the remembered row and not off the colony's answer, which carries no correlation at all
the row is gone (a restart, an `--apply` from outside) -> the receipt still goes out, with an empty id: the correlation is lost, the fact that the manifest was applied is not

a manifest whose `override_params` carries a `script_inline` -> a second check-only question with capability `code.author`, and `code_author_denied` while no enabled rule grants it; a manifest with no script asks no second question and costs no extra round trip

a manifest whose `add_edges` draws `{"modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_pack'"}}}` -> a third check-only question with capability `affinity.subscribe`, and `subscribe_not_permitted` while no enabled rule grants it

the same edge pointing at somebody else's hive -> `subscribe_target_not_self`, refused HERE and the broker never asked: a policy row does four one-sided comparisons and cannot compare the edge's target against the subject, so the gate secures the form and the broker answers only the capability question

an edge into a hive nobody in this manifest creates -> `subscribe_target_not_self` too: the second branch is about CREATION, so a parent may draw the door of the child it grows in the same declaration -- or of a rim inside that child, which is where the identity pack ends since GH #561 -- and of nothing else

an `add_nodes` entry naming `../dana/assistants/scribe`, or one that instantiates nothing at all (neither `template` nor `adopt`), used as the anchor of that edge -> `subscribe_target_not_self` as well: neither entry brings an addressee into the world under this declaration's scope, so neither anchors a door. An `adopt` entry does anchor -- it instantiates from a cell already on disk and mints a fresh id, which is a creation like any other (#566)

the same edge whose `from` is not an affinity hive -> `subscribe_source_not_affinity`. The hive PATH, never `<...>/affinity/push`: affinity's `params.ports` is empty, so an edge naming the port is refused at the door with `hive_port_boundary`

a committed manifest whose diff carried `add_templates` -> the receipt carries `registers_class: true` beside `applied`, and the shell's `./submit -> ./builder` edge turns it into the librarian's `in_ingest` nudge; the same manifest refused at the door carries the key too, with an `error_code` beside it, and that edge does not fire
